Facebook Shuttle Drivers Vote to Join a Union
search_results.description: On Wednesday, Facebook's shuttle-bus drivers voted to unionize in an effort to achieve higher wages and improved working conditions. The vote, reported by The Wall Street Journal, ended with 43 in favor and 28 opposed. Represented by Teamsters Local 853 in Northern California, the drivers are seeking changes to their current scheduling system, which requires them to work split shifts—two three-hour sessions in the morning and evening with a long six-hour break in between. The shuttle service is operated by Loop Transportation, which transports Facebook employees to and from the company’s Menlo Park headquarters. While Loop expressed reservations about the effectiveness of union representation, the company stated it would honor the drivers' decision and begin the negotiation process. Facebook declined to comment on the matter.
